title: Auth Gateway Event-Loop Freezing on CPU-Intensive Hashing
businessContext: During morning peak login hours (9:00 AM), an enterprise SSO authentication gateway suffers massive latency spikes. Simple GET `/health` probes jump from 2ms to 8,000ms, and ALB load balancers take instances out of service, causing cascading outages.
problemStatement: The password verification endpoint used synchronous `bcrypt.compareSync(password, hash)` with 14 salt rounds. Because Node.js is single-threaded on its JavaScript main thread, each synchronous hash blocks the entire event loop for 350ms. With 20 concurrent logins, all other incoming HTTP connections and TCP keep-alives are queued and frozen for over 7 seconds.
constraints: Must maintain high password hashing security parameters (e.g. bcrypt work factor 12-14 or Argon2id).
Event loop lag during concurrent logins must stay under 25ms.
candidateTasks: Explain how `bcrypt.compareSync` blocks the V8 thread vs how `bcrypt.compare` utilizes the libuv worker pool.
Explain the default size of `UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE` (4) and how to tune it for crypto-heavy Node applications.
hints: Synchronous crypto functions block the Node.js main thread completely.
Asynchronous crypto operations in Node.js are offloaded to libuv background thread pool (default 4 threads).
Set `process.env.UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE = 16` before starting the process if handling high concurrent crypto loads.

testCases.name: Uses libuv asynchronous thread pool without blocking event loop
testCases.explanation: Offloads CPU-intensive hashing to background worker threads.

alternativeApproaches: Offloading hashing to a dedicated microservice or Node.js Worker Threads (`worker_threads`).
Using Argon2id with WebAssembly / C bindings tuned for low iteration count and higher memory cost.
commonMistakes: Setting process.env.UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE after modules have already made async calls (libuv initializes the pool once and ignores later changes).
Thinking Promise.resolve().then(() => bcrypt.compareSync(...)) makes it non-blocking (it still runs synchronously on the main thread).
